(1) the singularity is covered if the mass function is bounded from below by a function that grows faster than R; (2) the singularity may either be covered or naked, depending on the behaviour of the mass at the singularity, if the mass function grows at least as fast as R; and (3) the singularity will be naked if the mass function does not grow faster than R.
the singularity is naked (covered) if the mass function M(R) grows faster (slower) than R, and is either naked or covered (depending on the mass function) if the two functions are proportional.
the central shell-focussing singularity in spherical collapse is naked for all mass functions m(R) such that m(R) = o(R).
